title: Linux setup lock: replace the non-darwin O_EXCL fallback with kernel-arbitrated locking (WCLI-20 review; prerequisite of WCLI-21)
description: src/adapters/setup-session.ts returns undefined from acquireFlock off darwin, so setup falls to an O_EXCL file with dead-pid reaping (clearStaleLock). The WCLI-20 review measured a check-then-delete race in that fallback: 12 overlapping holder pairs in 20 rounds, with process.platform faked. It is unreachable today only because the key provider refuses non-darwin (src/adapters/keychain.ts). WCLI-21 makes it reachable, so it must be replaced before any Linux key provider lands. The WCLI-20 note is recorded on WCLI-21 (grooming and review notes). Cleared by the leader on 2026-11-08 as the first slice of WCLI-21, independent of the TPM design questions.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On Linux the setup session lock is arbitrated by the kernel through bun:ffi on libc, with no new dependency, and the O_EXCL and dead-pid-reaping fallback is no longer used on Linux

A race test runs real overlapping holders, in separate processes and without faking process.platform, against the real lock and shows at most one holder at a time over many rounds of fresh one-shot processes behind a start barrier, the rounds on which the old fallback overlapped
The race test runs where Linux semantics are real (the Check job on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm runner), and the task says plainly which environments cannot run it
Any ADR amendment records this locking mechanism only, not the TPM design

ward-cli-review-294 verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES. opum-ai/ward-cli#294 (WCLI-152). The flock mechanism is correct, but the race test cannot tell the new lock from the old fallback, so AC1's second clause is not met.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- AC0 MET. Kernel-arbitrated flock through bun:ffi on libc, no new dependency, and no O_EXCL or dead-pid path left on Linux.
  - src/adapters/setup-session.ts:74-78: libcPath returns libSystem on darwin, libc.so.6 on linux, and throws vault_key_store_unsupported on anything else.
  - :103-113: a dlopen failure closes the fd and throws vault_store_failed.
  - :116-119: any non-zero flock result throws setup_in_progress.
  - acquireSetupSession (:150) always takes the flock path. There is no undefined return and no fallback branch.
  - package.json is unchanged. bun:ffi was already in use.
- AC1 NOT MET on the second clause ("the rounds on which the old fallback overlapped"). The first clause holds: real separate processes, no faked process.platform, the real lock, 4 x 150 rounds (test/setup.test.ts:433-487; test/fixtures/setup-lock-race-probe.ts). See finding 1.
- AC2 MET in substance, with two corrections owed in the task.
  - The Check job runs `bun run check`, which runs `bun test` (package.json:24-25), on a real Linux kernel (.github/workflows/ci.yml:57-72). The race tests and the formerly darwin-only "a live flock holder refuses a second setup, and release admits it" (skipIf removed, test/setup.test.ts:386) now run there unconditionally.
  - (a) The implementation note says "self-hosted Linux ARM64 CI job". ci.yml:47-59 runs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm (WCLI-99). The AC text is stale on the same point.
  - (b) The note says where the test ran, not where it cannot run. It needs one sentence naming those environments: macOS cannot exercise the Linux path; musl Linux (no libc.so.6) fails closed; every other platform fails closed with vault_key_store_unsupported.
  - I did not see the Check result on this SHA. Confirm it by the full SHA.
- AC3 MET. docs/adr/0001-vault-storage-and-key-custody.md:133-137 records the mechanism only: flock through libc.so.6, fail-closed rules, a race test with a no-lock control. Nothing about TPM.

FINDINGS
1. BLOCKING: test/setup.test.ts:475-486 ("with the lock no two holders ever overlap...") together with setup-lock-race-probe.ts:57-78. Predicted against the parent commit 316f566: this test passes against the old O_EXCL fallback in essentially every run, with overlaps == 0 and denied > 0.
   - How the old fallback overlapped: only through its reaping path. B reads holder A's pid, A releases and exits, C takes the lock, B finds A dead and rmSyncs C's file (the old clearStaleLock), then B takes a second lock.
   - Why this test cannot reach that path: the probes are long-lived loopers that always release before exiting. The pid B reads belongs to a live process, so clearStaleLock refuses and never reaps. The only openings are the 3 moments when a probe finishes its 150 rounds and exits, each microseconds wide.
   - The writer's no-op mutation shows the test catches a missing lock. It does not show the test catches the lock the AC names. The no-lock control is a real control of the detector, but it is a weaker baseline than the old fallback.
   - Fix: add a round shape like the WCLI-20 review's ("rounds of N simultaneous attempts", ADR 0001:128). Each round, spawn a batch of fresh one-shot processes behind a start barrier. Each takes the lock once, holds it, releases and exits, so dead recorded pids exist every round. Optionally also seed setup.lock with a dead pid, and have some holders exit or be killed while holding. Run 20 or more rounds with the same O_EXCL marker detector and the no-lock control.
   - Record one measurement of that harness against the parent fallback (platform faked for that one run only) showing overlaps > 0, so the test is proven able to fail on the thing it replaces.
   - The barrier also fixes finding 6.
2. Non-blocking: test/contract.test.ts:543-544. The comment on "setup_in_progress claims only what holds on every raise path" still justifies the wording partly through "the off-macOS fallback's clearStaleLock", which is now removed. The pinned wording still holds, because prepareVaultDirectory runs before the lock (setup-session.ts:145). Only the comment is stale.
3. Non-blocking: docs/adr/0001-vault-storage-and-key-custody.md:124-127. The paragraph still says, in the present tense, "Off macOS the fallback is an O_EXCL file...", and the amendment at :133 then says it is gone. A reader of the first sentence gets the wrong current state. Put that sentence in the past tense.
4. Non-blocking, a limit to state: the ward directory on NFS or CIFS. Linux emulates flock there with POSIX byte-range locks, so per-process semantics come back: two acquires in one process could both succeed, and the close at setup-session.ts:117 on a refused second acquire could drop the first holder's lock. Production takes one acquire per process (src/cli/main.ts:169), so this is unreachable today. Cross-host exclusion depends on NLM. On macOS, flock over SMB or NFS may return ENOTSUP, which reports as setup_in_progress: fails closed, but misleading. Worth one line in the ADR as a stated limit, because Linux home directories on NFS are common.
5. Non-blocking: musl Linux (Alpine). dlopen("libc.so.6") fails, and setup-session.ts:108-112 throws vault_store_failed. Safe, but the error does not say "unsupported libc". It also leaves an empty setup.lock behind, because the open at :95 runs before the dlopen. Harmless.
6. Non-blocking, flake risk: test/setup.test.ts:483 expects denied > 0, which assumes the 4 probes overlap in time. On a loaded runner, Bun start-up skew could serialize them and turn a correct lock red. A start barrier removes this.
7. Non-blocking, a check for WCLI-21: fd inheritance. The lock lives on the open file description, so a child spawned while it is held (for example tpm2-tools from a TPM provider) shares it if the fd lacks close-on-exec, and keeps it held after the parent exits. That costs liveness, not safety: it never lets two processes hold the lock. WCLI-21 should confirm that Bun's openSync sets O_CLOEXEC, or that its spawns close inherited fds.
8. Non-blocking, nit: setup-session.ts:105 calls dlopen and compiles a fresh FFI trampoline on every acquire and never closes it. Once per setup in production, 150 times per probe in tests.

VERIFIED CORRECT
- flock over fcntl F_SETLK: the writer's reasoning holds. Each acquire opens a fresh open file description (:95), so a second acquire in the same process conflicts with the first under flock. Under F_SETLK it would succeed, and the close at :117 would release the first holder's record lock.
- LOCK_EX=2 and LOCK_NB=4 (setup-session.ts:46-47) match glibc, musl and darwin <sys/file.h>. LOCK_UN is not needed because release is closeSync (:161-165), which drops the lock with the last reference to the description.
- The FFI signature (int, int) returning int matches `int flock(int, int)`, and fds fit in i32.
- No errno handling is needed: LOCK_NB never sleeps, so EINTR does not arise in practice, and any non-zero result fails closed as setup_in_progress.
- Release on every path: runSetup's finally (src/application/setup.ts:140-143) calls release unless complete() succeeded. complete() releases before its own fsync (:229-233). release is idempotent (:162). Kernel release on death is covered by the kill(9) test (test/setup.test.ts:402-408).
- Nothing in production or tests still references the removed isAlive, clearStaleLock, lockPid or removeOwnLock, or the O_EXCL lock path. The only mention left is the stale comment in finding 2.
- Scope: the diff touches only setup-session.ts, the two fixtures, setup.test.ts, ADR 0001 and the task record. No dependency is added and nothing about TPM appears.

IMPLEMENTATION 2026-11-08 (branch fix/WCLI-152-linux-setup-lock), round 1 fix. Mechanism: acquireFlock takes flock(2) through libc on darwin (libSystem) and linux (libc.so.6); the O_EXCL file, clearStaleLock, lockPid and compare-and-delete release are removed; any other platform fails closed (vault_key_store_unsupported), a missing C library as vault_store_failed. flock(2), not fcntl F_SETLK (POSIX record locks are per process and drop when any descriptor to the file closes). ROUND 1 FIX (finding 1): the race test is now 60 rounds, each a batch of 6 fresh one-shot processes behind a file start barrier; each takes the lock once, holds 3 ms and exits, odd-numbered ones exiting without release, over a setup.lock seeded each round with a reaped (dead) pid; a no-lock control must show overlaps. PROOF AGAINST THE OLD FALLBACK: the same test and probe, with only the probe faking process.platform=linux, run in a scratch worktree at parent 316f566cb8a281ecd95c7cedec8ddca0d3a1d552 (O_EXCL fallback live): overlaps 7, 3, 6, 6, 5 in five runs (all failed as intended). At 24 rounds it caught 2 of 3 runs and an earlier un-seeded long-lived-looper shape caught 0 of 3, hence 60 rounds and the seeding. On the new code the test passes 3 of 3 (about 13.5 s) and bun run check passes (1276 tests). WHERE IT RUNS: the Check job on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm runner (ci.yml, WCLI-99), a real Linux kernel; the reviewer-noted wording about a self-hosted runner was wrong. WHERE IT CANNOT RUN: macOS exercises only the darwin path and cannot run the Linux one; musl Linux (no libc.so.6) fails closed with vault_store_failed; every other platform fails closed with vault_key_store_unsupported; nothing of it ran on jetson. Non-blocking findings taken: 2 (stale contract.test.ts comment), 3 (ADR past tense), 4 (NFS/CIFS limit, one sentence in the ADR), 6 (the barrier removes the denied>0 flake). Left: 5 (musl wording), 8 (per-acquire dlopen), and 7 belongs to WCLI-21 slice 2.

APPROVE: round-2 verdict on opum-ai/ward-cli#294 (WCLI-152) at 0c99dbf53d7671aef673323b5da69a9f78d1c05a. Reviewer unit, read-only, nothing run. Round-1 finding 1 is fixed in the test's design, and I found nothing blocking.

ANSWERS TO (a) TO (e)

(a) Would the test fail against the old fallback?
- Parent 316f566 isn't readable from this checkout, so I reasoned from ADR 0001:124-127. It describes a recorded pid that is reaped only when provably dead, an empty or unreadable lock that is refused, and compare-and-delete release.
- The seed at test/setup.test.ts:457-461 writes a readable pid of a reaped process before every locked round. All 6 probes leave the barrier together, hit EEXIST, read the same dead pid and enter the reap branch at the same moment. That is the check-then-delete window: B removes the file A created after A's own reap, then creates its own, and both are inside the lock.
- The odd-index exit without release (probe:92) is secondary. It only matters for a probe that arrives late in the same round, after an odd holder has died.
- So the design does drive the old fallback into its reap race, and it supports the writer's claim. The overlap counts 7/3/6/6/5, the 2-of-3 result at 24 rounds, and the probe with the faked platform are NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THE CHECKOUT. That probe variant is not committed.
- Rough arithmetic on the claimed counts: about 5 detected overlaps per 60 rounds gives roughly a 0.5% chance that the old fallback would show 0. Those runs were presumably on the writer's machine, not the 4-vCPU hosted runner.

(b) Is the barrier sound?
- Yes. ready-<index> (probe:46) is written after every static import, including setup-session.ts, has been evaluated, so "ready" means "loaded".
- The remaining skew comes after `go`: prepareVaultDirectory, then dlopen and FFI trampoline compilation on every acquire (setup-session.ts:105, round-1 finding 8). That can exceed the 3 ms hold and serialize some rounds. It lowers contention per round. It cannot create a false overlap, and it cannot hide one.
- The busy spin (probe:48-50) can starve the parent's poll when the runner has fewer cores than BATCH+1. That slows the test but does not distort its result.

(c) Do the assertions prove exclusion without flaking?
- overlaps == 0 is a safety property and does not depend on timing.
- acquired >= ROUNDS is guaranteed. Each round awaits every probe's exit (:475-483) before the next seed. Linux closes a dying process's files before the parent is notified, so no flock is held when a round opens, and the first flock call wins.
- >= is the right operator. When an odd holder exits, the kernel releases its lock, so a late probe in the same round can also acquire, legitimately. == would be wrong.
- acquired >= ROUNDS also guards against a flock that always fails: everything would read as denied and acquired would be 0. A no-op flock would show up as overlaps, so the gate is covered both ways.
- denied > 0 is aggregated over 360 attempts, so it is not a realistic flake.
- acquired + denied == ROUNDS*BATCH is close to a tautology. Every probe acquires, is denied, or throws, and a throw fails at :480. Harmless.

(d) Are AC1 and AC2 met as worded?
- AC1: MET. The probes are real, separate, fresh one-shot processes; the platform is not faked; the lock is the real one; there are 60 rounds of 6 behind a start barrier; and there is a no-lock control (:493-501). The clause "the rounds on which the old fallback overlapped" holds by design as traced in (a). Its measured proof is a recorded claim in the task note.
- AC2: MET as worded. ci.yml:57-72 runs `bun run check` on ubuntu-24.04-arm, and that runs `bun test` (package.json:24-25). The race tests are not skipped. The task note and test/setup.test.ts:436-437 both state where it cannot run: macOS runs only the darwin path; musl Linux and every other platform fail closed.
- The Check result at 0c99dbf and its runner are your gh measurement, not mine.

(e) Does setup-session.ts match the ADR amendment?
- Yes. flock through libSystem on darwin and libc.so.6 on linux (:74-76). Any other platform fails closed with vault_key_store_unsupported (:77). A missing C library fails closed with vault_store_failed (:108-112). The file is never unlinked and holds the advisory pid (:121-126).
- No O_EXCL, clearStaleLock, isAlive, lockPid or removeOwnLock remains anywhere outside .quest/ (grep).

FINDINGS
1. Non-blocking. test/fixtures/setup-lock-race-probe.ts:48-50 and test/setup.test.ts:473: the barrier has no deadline on either side.
   - If one probe dies before it writes ready-<index> (an import error, say), the parent polls readdirSync until the 240 s timeout. It never checks worker.exitCode and never reads that probe's stderr, so the failure carries no diagnostic.
   - The other 5 probes spin on existsSync(go) forever. spawnProbe (:69-75) does not kill them, and afterAll's rmSync(root) makes `go` impossible to create. On a developer machine they stay as orphans at 100% CPU.
   - Suggested fix: a spin deadline in the probe (exit non-zero after about 30 s), and in the parent's ready loop, fail fast on a worker exit or a deadline.
2. Non-blocking. docs/adr/0001-vault-storage-and-key-custody.md:136: the NFS sentence is narrower than round-1 finding 4.
   - "exclusion there holds across processes only" leaves out that exclusion across hosts depends on NLM. A mount with locking disabled (nolock/local_lock) makes flock host-local.
   - On macOS, flock over SMB or NFS can return ENOTSUP, which reports as setup_in_progress.
   - Line 136 is also one unwrapped line of about 400 characters, where the rest of the paragraph wraps at about 100. That is a nit.
3. Non-blocking. The proof that the test can fail against the old fallback rests only on the task note. The probe variant with the faked platform is not committed. That is acceptable now that the fallback code is gone. If you want it re-measurable, keep the variant in the note's text, or as a disabled fixture.
4. Non-blocking, outside this diff. docs/adr/0004-committed-platform-target.md:49 still says "CI today is self-hosted Linux ARM64 only", and CLAUDE.md:66 says CI runs on `[self-hosted, Linux, ARM64]`. Both contradict ci.yml:47-59 (WCLI-99). Neither affects AC2. CLAUDE.md is the writer's governing file, so this is flagged for the owner, not asked of them.
5. Non-blocking, tracker hygiene. .quest/tasks/WCLI-152.json has status "To Do" while its PR is under review, and the SessionStart hook lists WCLI-120, WCLI-82 and WCLI-92 as In Progress but not WCLI-152. The writer may want it In Progress before finalization.

Not raised again: round-1 finding 7 (O_CLOEXEC, deferred to WCLI-21 slice 2), 5 (musl wording) and 8 (dlopen on every acquire), except as 8 bears on (b).

finalSummary: opum-ai/ward-cli#294 landed as fb08b92 on dev. The Linux setup lock is kernel-arbitrated flock(2) through libc (libc.so.6 on linux, libSystem on darwin); the O_EXCL file, dead-pid reaping and compare-and-delete release are removed; any other platform fails closed (vault_key_store_unsupported) and a missing C library as vault_store_failed. ADR 0001 records the mechanism only. Verified: a race test of 60 rounds of 6 fresh one-shot processes behind a start barrier over a dead-pid lock file, with a no-lock control; run against parent 316f566 with the platform faked in the probe it measured overlaps 7, 3, 6, 6, 5 in five runs (recorded in the implementation note); the Check job ran it on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm runner and passed on 0c99dbf, with Docs and Tracker integrity. Round 1 REQUEST_CHANGES (finding 1) was fixed; round 2 APPROVE from claude-opus-5-5. Where it cannot run: macOS runs only the darwin path; musl Linux and every other platform fail closed; nothing ran on jetson. Review non-blocking findings carried to a follow-up task (barrier deadline and orphan spinners; the NFS/NLM sentence and its line wrap) and to the CI-wording change (ADR 0004 and the profile); round-1 finding 7 (O_CLOEXEC) belongs to WCLI-21 slice 2.
